subject: storytime
title: The Little Engine That Could
about: Watty Piper's 1930 picture book about a train full of toys that breaks down, the big engines that will not help, and the little blue engine who says she thinks she can and pulls the toys over the mountain. First graders love chanting the refrain, and the story gives them words for trying hard at something new. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Chant I think I can, I think I can together while he pushes something heavy, like a box of books, across the room.

book.author: Watty Piper (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A little blue engine who thinks she can.

passage.text:
A little train was full of toys.
There were dolls and teddy bears.
There were toy trucks and red balls.
There were apples and oranges, too.
The toys were going to the good children.
The children lived on the other side of the mountain.
Then the train stopped.
Its engine would not go.
"Oh, no!" said the toys.
"How will we get over the mountain?"
***
A big shiny engine came by.
"Please pull us over the mountain," said the toys.
"I pull fancy trains," said the shiny engine.
"I will not pull toys."
And off it went.
Then a big strong engine came by.
"Please pull us over the mountain," said the toys.
"I pull heavy freight," said the strong engine.
"I will not pull toys."
And off it went.
The toys felt sad.
***
Then a little blue engine came by.
She was very small.
"Please pull us over the mountain," said the toys.
"I am not very big," she said.
"But the children need their toys."
"I think I can."
She hooked on to the little train.
Puff, puff! Chug, chug!
"I think I can. I think I can."
Up, up, up she went.
"I think I can. I think I can."
***
Slowly, slowly, she pulled the train up the mountain.
"I think I can. I think I can."
At last she got to the top!
"Hooray!" said the toys.
Then down the mountain she went.
"I thought I could. I thought I could."
The children got their toys.
They were so happy.
The little blue engine was happy, too.
Believe in yourself and try your best.

cards.q: What was the little train full of?
cards.note: Dolls, teddy bears, toy trucks, red balls, and apples and oranges too, all on their way to the children.

cards.q: Who were the toys going to?
cards.note: The good children lived on the other side of the mountain, which is why the train had to get over it.

cards.q: What did the big shiny engine pull?
cards.note: The shiny engine was too proud for toys, and the strong engine was too busy with its freight.

cards.q: What did the little blue engine say as she pulled?
cards.note: Say it with him, faster and faster, as the train climbs the mountain.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The engine would not go, so the toys were stuck at the foot of the mountain.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Down the other side of the mountain she went, saying I thought I could.

cards.q: How did the toys feel when the big engines left?
cards.note: Two big engines went off without them, so the toys felt sad until the little blue engine came.
Believe in yourself and try your best: the little engine was small, but she tried.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'freight' mean?
cards.note: Freight is the heavy load a train carries, like coal or boxes, and the strong engine pulled freight, not toys.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
